_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.
_why_unequal_followup: Follow-up runs from 0.5 to 5 years, so dividing events by PEOPLE instead of PERSON-TIME gives a different number, not a rescaled one.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process (a Poisson process at 0.08 per person-year)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same rate and the same exact interval bounds
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten decimals on every key. R's poisson.test and statsmodels' confint_poisson are independent implementations, and harness/descriptive_examples.test.py also checks the bounds against Garwood's chi-square formula.

recovery.claim: the estimated rate is close to the rate the fixture was built with

calibration.limits: Measured by harness/descriptive_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99. The committed fixture misses by 0.0103 (0.0903 against 0.08, about 1.4 standard errors).
